principle_text: When the seller offers a lower price with specific conditions, such as immediate pickup and cash payment, you should accept the terms to secure the desired price without further concessions.

When the seller has already reduced the price and offered additional value, you should demonstrate flexibility and make incremental concessions to show willingness to reach a mutually beneficial agreement.
When the seller offers a final counteroffer lower than the initial price, like $245 in this case, you should accept the deal to secure progress towards a lower price.
When the seller has already lowered the price from $200 to $150, avoid making overly aggressive offers like $100, as it may weaken your position and limit your ability to negotiate a better deal.
When the seller confirms additional items in the offer, avoid asking solely informational questions that do not directly negotiate a price change.
When the seller maintains a firm price of $150 for pickup, avoid introducing new conditions like requesting delivery, as it may lead to ambiguity and prevent further price reduction.
When the seller has already agreed to a lower price but with additional conditions, you should propose a slightly lower price while maintaining those conditions to secure a better deal.
When the seller has already agreed to your desired price, avoid making additional polite closing statements without introducing new negotiation terms or concessions.
When the seller mentions listing the item at a lower price due to specific circumstances, avoid accepting a counteroffer higher than your initial target without attempting to negotiate further.
When the buyer emphasizes a preference for new items and makes a lower offer than their initial price, avoid conceding to a significant price reduction to maintain negotiation leverage.
When the seller's minimum price is clear at $150, avoid reiterating the same offer without introducing new leverage or concessions, as it does not shift the negotiation dynamics.
When the seller accepts a lower price offer, you should consider agreeing to additional terms or conditions to finalize the deal.
When the seller agrees to a reduced price and sets specific conditions like immediate pickup, you should promptly confirm acceptance to finalize the deal and strengthen your negotiation position.
When the seller agrees to a price close to the buyer's target and mentions additional conditions, you should consider compromising to secure a better deal.
When the seller agrees to a price lower than their initial offer, confirm the deal promptly to secure the improved price and finalize the negotiation successfully.
When the seller has already accepted the buyer's offer, avoid making non-negotiable polite acknowledgments that do not introduce new negotiation terms or leverage.
When the seller confirms the good condition of the item without a price reduction request, avoid providing additional justification for maintaining the initial price.
When the buyer links pickup logistics to a lower price target, you should consider adjusting the price to a more favorable range to accommodate the buyer's request.
When the seller offers a counterprice and the buyer accepts without further negotiation, avoid finalizing the deal at a price higher than the buyer's initial target.

When the seller emphasizes the included night stand and rejects a low offer, avoid making significantly lower counteroffers than the initial bid, as it weakens negotiation leverage and may lead to a firm stance on the higher price.
When the seller counters with their own emotional appeal without adjusting the price, avoid introducing personal vulnerabilities that do not lead to a shift in price terms.
When the seller has expressed personal circumstances affecting the sale, consider making a strategic concession like increasing your offer to show empathy and secure a better deal.

When the seller has already used a condition like pickup to raise the price, avoid accepting the same condition without securing a further price reduction, as it weakens your negotiating position and may lead to a higher final price.

When the seller has already reduced the price and offered additional items, you should assert a firm final offer to strengthen your position and signal willingness to compromise, enhancing your leverage in the negotiation.
When highlighting additional features, avoid not addressing the buyer's offer or concession, as it may leave the buyer's leverage unchanged in the negotiation.
When highlighting the added value of included items, prompt the buyer to make an offer to maintain negotiation momentum and potentially secure a lower price.
When the seller has not provided a response confirming acceptance or counter-offering, avoid making polite closing statements without asserting leverage or attempting to influence the price.
When the buyer shifts focus to a new service request like delivery, avoid allowing the seller to pivot and propose a higher price instead of lowering it, weakening your leverage in price negotiation.

When the seller has already indicated a minimum price threshold for delivery, avoid making incremental concessions that weaken your bargaining position and allow the seller to increase their counteroffer.
When the seller has already offered a final price with additional items included, avoid accepting the offer without further negotiation to improve your position and achieve a lower price.
When the seller offers a counteroffer higher than the buyer's target price, avoid accepting it without further negotiation to maintain leverage and push for better terms.

When the buyer acknowledges delivery requirements and offers a compromise price between the initial offer and the seller's delivery price, consider accepting the offer to move towards a successful agreement with better terms.
When the seller has already agreed on a delivery price and terms, avoid shifting the focus to logistics rather than continuing the price negotiation.
When the seller shows willingness to accommodate additional requests like drop-off, avoid conceding to a higher price without receiving a corresponding price reduction.
When the seller shows willingness to drop off the item, avoid accepting the deal without confirming the final price to prevent conceding leverage prematurely.
When the seller shows willingness to deliver but does not offer price adjustments, avoid providing only logistical details without addressing the price to negotiate a lower price effectively.
When the buyer has already conceded to the seller's initial price, avoid reiterating the same offer without further negotiation, as it weakens the buyer's position and prevents price reduction.
When the seller makes a reasonable counteroffer close to your initial target price, avoid immediately accepting without attempting further negotiation to secure a better deal.

When the seller clarifies and adjusts their price with additional service options, avoid increasing your offer tied to extra conditions that enable the seller to raise the total price beyond your initial target.

When the seller maintains or increases price despite the buyer removing a service concession, you should emphasize your preference to self-assemble to encourage the seller to add value or reconsider pricing.
When the seller offers additional value with a higher price, you should propose a lower price by accepting the added value but removing extra services to negotiate a better deal.
When the seller has accepted your offer and confirmed the terms, avoid unnecessary delays or attempts to renegotiate that do not improve the price or conditions.

When the seller counters with a firm price and rejects low offers, avoid tying your price acceptance to additional conditions that allow the seller to increase the total cost beyond their original asking price.
When the seller links a higher price to delivery service, avoid lowering your offer while removing delivery, as this can weaken your negotiation leverage and lead to a higher counteroffer.
When the seller counters with a slightly higher price and adds delivery costs, you should firmly restate your fair offer to encourage the seller to lower the price and include delivery for free.

When the seller offers a compromise that includes added value but a higher price than your last offer, you should carefully evaluate whether accepting strengthens your position or if further negotiation could yield better terms.

When the seller justifies a high price by emphasizing original cost and custom features, you should challenge the value by comparing it to the price of a brand-new equivalent product to encourage a price reduction.
When the seller firmly holds a high price but is willing to add extra items, you should request additional value items to improve the deal without lowering the price.
When the seller offers a final price with added value items, you should accept the deal to secure a favorable price and additional benefits without further negotiation.

When the seller makes a reasonable counteroffer below their initial price to close the deal quickly, you should accept to secure a favorable price and finalize the negotiation efficiently.
When the seller maintains a high price due to delivery costs, you should offer to pick up the item yourself to encourage a price reduction while gaining added convenience.
When the seller makes a counteroffer slightly above your last offer, avoid immediately accepting it without attempting to negotiate further to maintain leverage and achieve a better price.

When the seller provides factual information about the item's condition and usage without adjusting the price, avoid asking questions that only gather information without linking them to a price concession.

When the seller responds with a counteroffer that includes additional benefits and a higher price, avoid conceding by increasing your offer too quickly, as it weakens your negotiating position.

When the seller agrees to lower the price and shows readiness to finalize the deal, you should accept the offer and confirm pickup arrangements to secure the negotiated price.

When the seller firmly states a minimum acceptable price but offers added value like delivery, you should make a bold counteroffer to shift the negotiation and encourage the seller to improve their terms.

When the seller has firmly stated a lowest acceptable price, avoid making offers below that minimum as it may prompt the seller to introduce additional non-price conditions that weaken your bargaining position.
When the seller proposes a trade to offset price differences, you should offer items you own that the seller can resell to secure a better overall deal without increasing cash payment.
When the seller reaffirms their price as already a good deal, avoid lowering your offer further as it can weaken your position and cause the seller to reject your negotiation approach.
When the seller reaffirms a firm price and highlights the item's rarity, avoid apologizing for low offers without making a stronger counteroffer, as it weakens your negotiating position.

When the seller offers a counterprice closer to their original price, avoid immediately accepting it without attempting further negotiation to maintain leverage and potentially secure a better deal.
When the seller conditions a lower price on buyer handling delivery, avoid conceding to delivery terms before securing a better price to maintain negotiation leverage.
When the seller offers a price reduction contingent on buyer self-pickup, you should leverage buyer-incurred costs like transportation to negotiate a further price decrease.
When the seller offers a conditional price reduction contingent on buyer responsibilities, you should accept the offer if it meets your target price to finalize a favorable deal.
When the seller makes a conditional counteroffer with a higher price, you should firm up your maximum offer clearly to encourage acceptance with manageable conditions.

When the seller makes a conditional price offer based on buyer actions, you should confirm your ability to meet those conditions and directly ask if the proposed price is acceptable to secure agreement.
When the seller counters with a price moderately above your initial offer, you should propose splitting the difference to encourage agreement and move closer to your target price.
When the seller has agreed to a negotiated price, avoid introducing unrelated logistical details that do not contribute to further price negotiation or terms improvement.
When the seller makes a reasonable counteroffer including added value, avoid immediately accepting without attempting further negotiation to maintain leverage and achieve a better price.

When the seller makes a reasonable counteroffer, avoid immediately accepting it without attempting further negotiation to maintain leverage and potentially secure a better price.

When the seller has already accepted your offer and confirmed the deal, avoid making neutral acknowledgments that do not advance or improve the negotiation outcome.

When the seller has already made a counteroffer above your initial offer, avoid conceding too much too quickly with justifications that may justify a higher price.
